title: The Office - Interview Skills 5 - Discussing Reasons For Leaving Previous Position
audio: mp3/247. The Office - Interview Skills 5 - Discussing Reasons For Leaving Previous Position.mp3

segments.en: Hello everyone and welcome to EnglishPod.
segments.zh: 大家好，欢迎来到 EnglishPod。

segments.en: My name is Marco.
segments.zh: 我叫 Marco。

segments.en: My name is Catherine and today we're going to continue in our series about job interviews.
segments.zh: 我的名字是凯瑟琳，今天我们将继续我们关于工作面试的系列。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: And on this occasion we're taking a look at part five of our interview series where we explain why we left our previous job.
segments.zh: 这一次，我们要看的是面试系列的第五部分，讲的是如何解释我们为什么离开上一份工作。

segments.en: Okay, and so in an interview, this is a very popular question.
segments.zh: 好的，所以面试中，这是一个非常常见的问题。

segments.en: Why did you leave your last job?
segments.zh: 你为什么离开你的上一份工作？

segments.en: Learn some tools for answering this question in today's dialogue.
segments.zh: 在今天的对话中学习一些回答这个问题的工具。

segments.en: We're going to take a listen to it first and we'll be back in a moment.
segments.zh: 我们要先听一听，我们一会儿就回来。

segments.en: Okay, now I'd like to find out more about your last job.
segments.zh: 好的，现在我想了解更多关于你上一份工作的信息。

segments.en: I see you spent almost four years at the London Weekly.
segments.zh: 我看到你在《伦敦周刊》待了将近四年。

segments.en: Is that right?
segments.zh: 是这样吗？

segments.en: Yes, that's right.
segments.zh: 对，没错。

segments.en: To be honest, the first year was quite tough for me.
segments.zh: 老实说，第一年对我来说相当艰难。

segments.en: I was really just treated more like an intern.
segments.zh: 我真的只是被当作实习生对待。

segments.en: I didn't have many responsibilities and I found it quite frustrating.
segments.zh: 我没有太多的责任，我觉得这很令人沮丧。

segments.en: So, what changed?
segments.zh: 那么，发生了什么变化？

segments.en: Well, slowly but surely I proved myself and the new editor liked me so he promoted me to Features Writer.
segments.zh: 后来我逐渐证明了自己的能力，新主编很欣赏我，便把我提拔为专题记者。

segments.en: Wow, a real step up.
segments.zh: 哇，一个真正的进步。

segments.en: Yes, I was responsible for restaurant and food reviews mostly.
segments.zh: 是的，我主要负责餐厅和食品评论。

segments.en: I spent three years in that position.
segments.zh: 我在那个职位上呆了三年。

segments.en: But to be honest, it wasn't an area of journalism I wanted to stay in long term.
segments.zh: 不过说实话，我不想长期从事这一类新闻报道。

segments.en: I see.
segments.zh: 我明白了。

segments.en: So why did you decide to leave finally?
segments.zh: 那你为什么决定最终离开呢？

segments.en: I just felt that the paper couldn't offer me any new opportunities.
segments.zh: 我只是觉得那家报社已经无法给我新的发展机会。

segments.en: I really needed a more challenging role to be honest.
segments.zh: 说实话，我确实需要一份更有挑战性的工作。

segments.en: Alright, we're back and as we saw, Rebecca handled it quite well explaining why you left your last job because obviously you don't want to say something like, I just really didn't like my company or the boss was a really bad guy.
segments.zh: 好吧，我们回来了，正如我们所见，丽贝卡很好地解释了你为什么离开上一份工作，因为显然你不想说这样的话，我只是真的不喜欢我的公司或老板是一个非常坏的人。

segments.en: Or I was fired for being lazy.
segments.zh: 或者我因为懒惰而被解雇。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: So, why don't we take a look at a couple of different words on Language Takeaway.
segments.zh: 那么，我们为什么不看看语言要点的几个不同的词。

segments.en: Language Takeaway.
segments.zh: 语言要点。

segments.en: Okay, so we've got some great descriptive words here.
segments.zh: 好的，所以我们在这里有一些很棒的描述性词。

segments.en: These are some adjectives.
segments.zh: 这些是一些形容词。

segments.en: The first one is tough.
segments.zh: 第一个是艰难的。

segments.en: So Rebecca said, to be honest, the first year was quite tough for me.
segments.zh: 所以丽贝卡说，老实说，第一年对我来说相当艰难。

segments.en: Alright, so she's describing that her first year at that company where she was working, it was tough and that means hard, difficult.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以她描述了她在那家公司工作的第一年，这很艰难，这意味着艰难、困难。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: You could say, this is a really tough situation.
segments.zh: 你可以说，这是一个非常艰难的情况。

segments.en: That means it's a difficult situation.
segments.zh: 这意味着这是一个困难的情况。

segments.en: It's hard because there's no easy answer.
segments.zh: 这很难，因为没有简单的答案。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: So, if you describe something as tough, it means that it's very difficult.
segments.zh: 所以，如果你把某件事描述为艰难的话，这意味着它非常困难。

segments.en: Now there is another meaning to this where it can be that you are a strong person.
segments.zh: 这个词还有另一个含义，可以指你是一个坚强的人。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So that's different because we're talking about a person, not a situation.
segments.zh: 所以这是不同的，因为我们谈论的是一个人，而不是一个情况。

segments.en: But if you're talking about a job or an experience or even homework, like this homework is really tough, it means that it's very hard.
segments.zh: 但如果你在谈论工作、经历甚至家庭作业，比如这个家庭作业真的很艰难，这意味着它非常困难。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: So apart from her job being a little bit tough, she said that it was also a little bit frustrating.
segments.zh: 所以除了她的工作有点艰难之外，她说这也有点令人沮丧。

segments.en: Okay, so usually these things go together.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以这些东西通常会在一起。

segments.en: If something is tough, like it's difficult, it's usually frustrating too.
segments.zh: 如果某事很艰难，很难，它通常也会令人沮丧。

segments.en: So in this case, something is frustrating when it makes you unhappy or for example, it makes you feel stressed.
segments.zh: 所以在这种情况下，当它让你不开心时，它会令人沮丧，或者例如，它会让你感到压力。

segments.en: So something that's frustrating is not a good thing.
segments.zh: 所以令人沮丧的事情并不是一件好事。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: So as you gave the example with the homework assignment, if you have maybe a math assignment that's very difficult and you can't solve it, you don't find the solution, then you get frustrated.
segments.zh: 所以就像你举的作业这个例子，假如你的数学作业非常难，你解不出来，找不到答案，就会感到沮丧。

segments.en: You get maybe angry at yourself or you get very angry for not being able to solve it.
segments.zh: 你可能会生自己的气，或者你因为无法解决它而感到非常生气。

segments.en: So that's when something is frustrating.
segments.zh: 所以这就是当事情令人沮丧的时候。

segments.en: I hate being frustrated.
segments.zh: 我讨厌沮丧。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: Well, it's not a nice feeling.
segments.zh: 嗯，这不是一种好感觉。

segments.en: But she said that, well, it was frustrating, it was tough, but after a while, I proved myself.
segments.zh: 但她说，好吧，这很令人沮丧，这很艰难，但过了一段时间，我证明了自己。

segments.en: Okay, so that means that she was able to show someone that she can handle difficult things, difficult work, difficult situations.
segments.zh: 好吧，这意味着她能够向某人表明她可以处理困难的事情、困难的工作、困难的情况。

segments.en: And so she said, I proved myself and the new editor liked me.
segments.zh: 所以她说，我证明了自己，新编辑喜欢我。

segments.en: So basically, she did a really good job.
segments.zh: 所以基本上，她做得非常好。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: So if you prove yourself, you're showing someone that you have great ability or capabilities of solving a problem or being able to handle a difficult job.
segments.zh: 所以，如果你能证明自己，你就是在向别人表明，你有很强的能力，能解决问题，或者能胜任困难的工作。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So you could say, last year, Bob didn't do very well at school, but this year, he really proved himself.
segments.zh: 所以你可以说，去年，鲍勃在学校表现不佳，但今年，他真的证明了自己。

segments.en: He studied hard and he got really good grades.
segments.zh: 他努力学习，取得了非常好的成绩。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: And well, Rebecca, what she got in exchange for proving herself, she got promoted.
segments.zh: 而丽贝卡证明自己，换来的回报就是得到了晋升。

segments.en: This is great.
segments.zh: 这太棒了。

segments.en: So promotions are good things.
segments.zh: 所以晋升是好事。

segments.en: The verb here is to promote or to be promoted.
segments.zh: 这里的动词是 promote（提拔），或者说 be promoted（被提拔）。

segments.en: So in this case, she was promoted.
segments.zh: 所以在这种情况下，她被提拔了。

segments.en: You could say, last year, I was promoted or he will be promoted next week.
segments.zh: 你可以说，去年我升职了，或者他下周会升职。

segments.en: He doesn't know yet.
segments.zh: 他还不知道。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: Now, remember that to be promoted means to get a better position in your job.
segments.zh: 现在，请记住，升职意味着在您的工作中获得更好的职位。

segments.en: Now, as we mentioned, the verb is to promote and you may be asking yourself why we are using the verb to be in the past, was promoted.
segments.zh: 现在，正如我们提到的，动词是 promote，你可能会问自己，为什么我们在这里用的是 be 的过去式 was promoted。

segments.en: And this is because it's an ed adjective.
segments.zh: 这是因为它是一个ed形容词。

segments.en: It's an adjective that ends in ed.
segments.zh: 这是一个以ed结尾的形容词。

segments.en: So you may think it's a verb, but it's not.
segments.zh: 所以你可能认为它是一个动词，但事实并非如此。

segments.en: It's actually an adjective.
segments.zh: 它实际上是一个形容词。

segments.en: The verb here is to be.
segments.zh: 这里的动词是 be。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: So I was promoted.
segments.zh: 于是我升职了。

segments.en: So was is obviously our verb here, the verb to be, but promoted is an adjective that ends in ed.
segments.zh: 所以 was 显然是这里的主要动词，也就是 be 的过去式，但 promoted 是一个以 ed 结尾的形容词。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: And so if I'm the boss, the action I do, the verb I do is I promote someone.
segments.zh: 所以如果我是老板，我做的动作，我做的动词就是提拔某人。

segments.en: So this can be a little bit tricky, but we recommend that you check out the website for more details because we have lots of examples of how to use this.
segments.zh: 所以这可能有点棘手，但我们建议您查看网站以获取更多详细信息，因为我们有很多如何使用它的示例。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: Well, she got promoted and well, she was really happy for a while, but then she said, you know what, I really needed a more challenging role, a more challenging job.
segments.zh: 好吧，她得到了晋升，也开心了一阵子，但后来她说，你知道吗，我真的需要一个更有挑战性的角色，一份更有挑战性的工作。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: Challenging is a great adjective.
segments.zh: Challenging 是一个很好的形容词。

segments.en: It means something is difficult or it gives you a challenge.
segments.zh: 这意味着有些事情很困难，或者它给你一个挑战。

segments.en: So that means it's not easy.
segments.zh: 所以这意味着这并不容易。

segments.en: Yeah.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So she found that her job was a little bit too easy.
segments.zh: 所以她发现她的工作有点太容易了。

segments.en: So she wanted something a little bit more challenging.
segments.zh: 所以她想要一些更具挑战性的东西。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: And so this is a really great word for job interviews in particular, because you're basically saying, I want hard work.
segments.zh: 所以这个词在工作面试中尤其好用，因为你基本上是在说，我愿意做辛苦的工作。

segments.en: I want to prove myself.
segments.zh: 我想证明自己。

segments.en: There we go again.
segments.zh: 我们又来了。

segments.en: So I want to show you that I'm a good employee or a hard worker.
segments.zh: 所以我想向你展示我是一个好员工或一个勤奋的人。

segments.en: And so I want a challenge, something that's hard.
segments.zh: 所以我想要一个挑战，一些困难的事情。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: So something that is hard is a challenge or you want something challenging.
segments.zh: 所以很难的事情是一个挑战，或者你想要一些具有挑战性的东西。

segments.en: So why don't we review these words that we've taken a look at now.
segments.zh: 那么我们为什么不回顾一下我们现在看过的这些词。

segments.en: Let's go back to the dialogue and listen to it again.
segments.zh: 让我们回到对话并再次聆听。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: Now I'd like to find out more about your last job.
segments.zh: 现在我想了解更多关于你上一份工作的信息。

segments.en: I see you spent almost four years at the London Weekly.
segments.zh: 我看到你在《伦敦周刊》待了将近四年。

segments.en: Is that right?
segments.zh: 是这样吗？

segments.en: Yes, that's right.
segments.zh: 对，没错。

segments.en: To be honest, the first year was quite tough for me.
segments.zh: 老实说，第一年对我来说相当艰难。

segments.en: I was really just treated more like an intern.
segments.zh: 我真的只是被当作实习生对待。

segments.en: I didn't have many responsibilities and I found it quite frustrating.
segments.zh: 我没有太多的责任，我觉得这很令人沮丧。

segments.en: So what changed?
segments.zh: 那么发生了什么变化？

segments.en: Well slowly but surely I proved myself and the new editor liked me.
segments.zh: 好吧，慢慢地，我证明了自己，新编辑也喜欢我。

segments.en: So he promoted me to features writer.
segments.zh: 所以他把我提拔为专题记者。

segments.en: Wow.
segments.zh: 哇。

segments.en: A real step up.
segments.zh: 真正的进步。

segments.en: Yes.
segments.zh: 是的。

segments.en: I was responsible for restaurant and food reviews.
segments.zh: 我负责餐厅和食品评论。

segments.en: Mostly I spent three years in that position.
segments.zh: 主要是我在那个职位上呆了三年。

segments.en: But to be honest, it wasn't an area of journalism I wanted to stay in long term.
segments.zh: 不过说实话，我不想长期从事这一类新闻报道。

segments.en: I see.
segments.zh: 我明白了。

segments.en: So why did you decide to leave finally?
segments.zh: 那你为什么决定最终离开呢？

segments.en: I just felt that the paper couldn't offer me any new opportunities.
segments.zh: 我只是觉得那家报社已经无法给我新的发展机会。

segments.en: I really needed a more challenging role to be honest.
segments.zh: 说实话，我确实需要一份更有挑战性的工作。

segments.en: All right, we're back.
segments.zh: 好了，我们回来了。

segments.en: So now let's take a look at a couple of phrases we picked out for you on Fluency Builder.
segments.zh: 所以现在让我们来看看我们在流利表达上为你挑选的几个短语。

segments.en: Fluency Builder.
segments.zh: 流利表达。

segments.en: Okay, this first phrase is unusual because it actually happens at the end of sentences.
segments.zh: 好的，第一个短语是不寻常的，因为它实际上发生在句子的末尾。

segments.en: This is very, very common with people who are making small talk or who are doing interviews.
segments.zh: 这在那些正在闲聊或进行采访的人中非常非常常见。

segments.en: This is the phrase, is that right?
segments.zh: 这是这句话，对吗？

segments.en: So basically you saw that in the first line Mr. Parsons was talking to her and said, well, I see you spent almost four years at the London Weekly.
segments.zh: 所以基本上你在第一行看到帕森斯先生正在和她说话，并说，好吧，我看到你在伦敦周刊上花了将近四年的时间。

segments.en: Is that right?
segments.zh: 是这样吗？

segments.en: So he's ending the sentence with this phrase.
segments.zh: 所以他用这个短语结束了句子。

segments.en: So he's making the sentence a question.
segments.zh: 所以他把这句话当成了一个问题。

segments.en: I see that you did this.
segments.zh: 我看到你这样做了。

segments.en: Is that right?
segments.zh: 是这样吗？

segments.en: So he's asking her to confirm the fact that he knows about her because maybe they've never really talked before.
segments.zh: 所以他要求她确认他了解她的事实，因为也许他们以前从未真正交谈过。

segments.en: So this is a good way for him to ask her to give more details.
segments.zh: 所以这是他要求她提供更多细节的好方法。

segments.en: So for example, Marco, I hear that you're from Ecuador.
segments.zh: 例如，Marco，我听说你来自厄瓜多尔。

segments.en: Is that right?
segments.zh: 是这样吗？

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So apart from ending the sentence like this, if maybe somebody asks you, is that right?
segments.zh: 所以除了像这样结束这句话，如果有人问你，对吗？

segments.en: You have to confirm.
segments.zh: 你必须确认。

segments.en: You have to say, yes, that's right.
segments.zh: 你必须说，是的，这是对的。

segments.en: Or yes.
segments.zh: 或者是的。

segments.en: It's also good to elaborate, to give more details.
segments.zh: 详细说明也很好，提供更多细节。

segments.en: So yes, I'm from Ecuador.
segments.zh: 所以是的，我来自厄瓜多尔。

segments.en: I was born there, but I've lived in the United States.
segments.zh: 我出生在那里，但我住在美国。

segments.en: This is a way to give more information because that's basically what the person's asking.
segments.zh: 这是一种提供更多信息的方式，因为这基本上是这个人的要求。

segments.en: Yeah, I think it wouldn't be very good if you're at a job interview and the person says, is that right?
segments.zh: 是的，我认为如果你在工作面试中并且这个人说，对吗？

segments.en: And you say, yes, that's right.
segments.zh: 你说，是的，这是对的。

segments.en: And then you don't say anything else.
segments.zh: 然后你什么都不说。

segments.en: So yeah, basically the point is you have to confirm or deny.
segments.zh: 所以，是的，基本上关键是你必须确认或否认。

segments.en: You have to say, yes, that's right or no, that's not right.
segments.zh: 你必须说，是的，没错，或者不，那不对。

segments.en: And then you have to give some information about the question.
segments.zh: 然后你必须提供一些关于这个问题的信息。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: Now, moving on, when Rebecca again was talking about her job, she was saying it's tough and I didn't have many responsibilities and I found it quite frustrating.
segments.zh: 现在，接下来，丽贝卡再次谈到她的工作时，她说工作很艰难，我没有太多责任，我觉得很令人沮丧。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So this is like lost and found.
segments.zh: 所以这就像失物招领处。

segments.en: Like I lost my hat and I found it later.
segments.zh: 就像我丢了帽子，后来我找到了它。

segments.en: No, no.
segments.zh: 不，不。

segments.en: This is what's interesting about this verb, find.
segments.zh: 这就是 find 这个动词有趣的地方。

segments.en: We are not actually looking for something or we didn't actually find something we were looking for.
segments.zh: 我们实际上并不是在寻找什么东西，或者我们实际上并没有找到我们正在寻找的东西。

segments.en: This is kind of a realization, right?
segments.zh: 这是一种认识，对吧？

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: It's like a feeling.
segments.zh: 这就像一种感觉。

segments.en: So I find this movie boring.
segments.zh: 所以我觉得这部电影很无聊。

segments.en: That means I think this movie is boring.
segments.zh: 这意味着我认为这部电影很无聊。

segments.en: It's the way that you're thinking about something.
segments.zh: 这是你思考某事的方式。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: Or you can say, oh, I found Paris to be quite an expensive city.
segments.zh: 或者你可以说，哦，我发现巴黎是一个相当昂贵的城市。

segments.en: Yeah, pretty expensive.
segments.zh: 是的，很贵。

segments.en: So this is your impression.
segments.zh: 所以这是你的印象。

segments.en: This is the way that you feel about something.
segments.zh: 这就是你对某事的感受。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: So this is another way that you can use this word to find.
segments.zh: 所以这是 find 这个词的另一种用法。

segments.en: Now again, when Rebecca talked about proving herself, she used a very interesting, I would say phrase, a very popular well-known phrase, slowly but surely.
segments.zh: 再一次，当丽贝卡谈到证明自己时，她用了一个非常有意思的说法，一个非常流行、众所周知的短语：slowly but surely。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So slowly but surely is the opposite of right away.
segments.zh: 所以 slowly but surely 和 right away（立刻）意思相反。

segments.en: Right?
segments.zh: 对吧？

segments.en: So something that happens right away is immediate.
segments.zh: 所以立即发生的事情是立即发生的。

segments.en: Like I got promoted right away.
segments.zh: 就像我马上升职一样。

segments.en: But slowly but surely means after lots of time and even hard work, this good thing happened.
segments.zh: 但 slowly but surely 意味着经过很长时间，甚至付出辛苦努力之后，这件好事才发生。

segments.en: Or it's usually a good thing, actually.
segments.zh: 或者这通常是一件好事，实际上。

segments.en: Yeah.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: You're basically saying that you didn't do anything very quickly, but you did it very well.
segments.zh: 你基本上是说你没有很快做任何事情，但你做得很好。

segments.en: So slowly but surely, I finished building my home.
segments.zh: 就这样慢慢地，我把房子盖好了。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So it didn't happen overnight, but it did happen over time.
segments.zh: 所以它不是一夜之间发生的，但它确实随着时间的推移而发生。

segments.en: You can also say this about studying a language.
segments.zh: 你也可以这样说是关于学习一种语言。

segments.en: At the beginning, learning English was really hard, but slowly but surely, I became fluent.
segments.zh: 一开始，学英语真的很难，但我慢慢地、一步步地变得流利了。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So slowly but surely.
segments.zh: 所以就是 slowly but surely。

segments.en: And the last phrase that we have for you today, you may have seen that Rebecca used this phrase, to be honest, a couple of times before explaining something.
segments.zh: 今天要讲的最后一个短语，你可能注意到丽贝卡在解释某件事之前用了几次，to be honest。

segments.en: So why does she say to be honest?
segments.zh: 那么她为什么说说实话呢？

segments.en: To be honest is sometimes something we say in English to fill some space or some time.
segments.zh: To be honest 有时候是我们在英语里用来填补空档或争取时间的话。

segments.en: We call it filler.
segments.zh: 我们称之为填充词。

segments.en: But it's also a way to introduce something that's negative.
segments.zh: 但这也是一种引入负面事物的方式。

segments.en: So for example, in this dialogue, she's talking about her negative experiences.
segments.zh: 因此，例如，在这次对话中，她谈论的是她的负面经历。

segments.en: My job was tough.
segments.zh: 我的工作很艰难。

segments.en: My experience was bad.
segments.zh: 我的经历很糟糕。

segments.en: So she says, to be honest, it wasn't the best experience, but I learned from it.
segments.zh: 所以她说，老实说，这不是最好的经历，但我从中吸取了教训。

segments.en: She's saying this to introduce some things that are maybe not positive, not happy things.
segments.zh: 她这么说是为了介绍一些可能不积极、不快乐的事情。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So it's another way of saying, look, I'm going to tell you the truth.
segments.zh: 所以这是另一种说法，看，我要告诉你真相。

segments.en: It may not be something positive, but this is what happened.
segments.zh: 这可能不是积极的事情，但这就是发生的事情。

segments.en: So to be honest, I didn't really like my last employer or something like that.
segments.zh: 所以老实说，我真的不喜欢我的上一个雇主或类似的东西。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: We can even talk about this with your friends.
segments.zh: 我们甚至可以和你的朋友讨论这个问题。

segments.en: So hey, Marco, did you like that movie Shutter Island?
segments.zh: 嘿，马可，你喜欢那个电影快门岛吗？

segments.en: To be honest, I didn't really see it.
segments.zh: 老实说，我其实没看过。

segments.en: Oh.
segments.zh: 哦。

segments.en: I fell asleep.
segments.zh: 我睡着了。

segments.en: Or you could say, to be honest, I didn't love it.
segments.zh: 或者你可以说，老实说，我不喜欢它。

segments.en: I didn't really like it.
segments.zh: 我真的不喜欢它。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: So it's a very good phrase, but don't overuse it.
segments.zh: 所以这是一个很好的短语，但不要过度使用它。

segments.en: I think sometimes you get into the habit of using it all the time and just like, like, you know, well, you know, like I went to the movies like yesterday, like, and like, to be honest, like, so try to keep these fillers as you described them to a minimum.
segments.zh: 我想有时候你会养成一直用它的习惯，就像、就像，你知道，嗯，你知道，就像我昨天去看电影，like，然后 like，说实话，like，所以尽量把这些填充词控制到最少，就像你说的那样。

segments.en: So don't really use them too much.
segments.zh: 所以不要真的用太多。

segments.en: Yes.
segments.zh: 是的。

segments.en: Say thoughts and ideas.
segments.zh: 说出想法和观点。

segments.en: Nice action verbs, not too much fillers, because sometimes, especially in an interview, it makes people think that you don't really know much to say.
segments.zh: 用些好的动词，别用太多填充词，因为有时，尤其是在面试中，会让人觉得你没什么可说的。

segments.en: Yeah, exactly.
segments.zh: 对，没错。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So listen to the dialogue for the last time and we'll be back to chat a little bit more.
segments.zh: 所以最后一次听对话，我们会再聊一会儿。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: Now I'd like to find out more about your last job.
segments.zh: 现在我想了解更多关于你上一份工作的信息。

segments.en: I see you spent almost four years at the London Weekly.
segments.zh: 我看到你在《伦敦周刊》待了将近四年。

segments.en: Is that right?
segments.zh: 是这样吗？

segments.en: Yes, that's right.
segments.zh: 对，没错。

segments.en: To be honest, the first year was quite tough for me.
segments.zh: 老实说，第一年对我来说相当艰难。

segments.en: I was really just treated more like an intern.
segments.zh: 我真的只是被当作实习生对待。

segments.en: I didn't have many responsibilities and I found it quite frustrating.
segments.zh: 我没有太多的责任，我觉得这很令人沮丧。

segments.en: So what changed?
segments.zh: 那么发生了什么变化？

segments.en: Well slowly but surely I proved myself and the new editor liked me so he promoted me to Features Writer.
segments.zh: 好吧，缓慢但肯定地证明了我自己，新编辑喜欢我，所以他把我提升为专题作家。

segments.en: Wow, a real step up.
segments.zh: 哇，一个真正的进步。

segments.en: Yes, I was responsible for restaurant and food reviews mostly.
segments.zh: 是的，我主要负责餐厅和食品评论。

segments.en: I spent three years in that position.
segments.zh: 我在那个职位上呆了三年。

segments.en: But to be honest, it wasn't an area of journalism I wanted to stay in long term.
segments.zh: 不过说实话，我不想长期从事这一类新闻报道。

segments.en: I see.
segments.zh: 我明白了。

segments.en: So why did you decide to leave finally?
segments.zh: 那你为什么决定最终离开呢？

segments.en: I just felt that the paper couldn't offer me any new opportunities.
segments.zh: 我只是觉得那家报社已经无法给我新的发展机会。

segments.en: I really needed a more challenging role to be honest.
segments.zh: 说实话，我确实需要一份更有挑战性的工作。

segments.en: Alright so talking about your last employer, this is a pretty ideal thing.
segments.zh: 好吧，说到上一份工作的雇主，这可以说是一个很理想的答法。

segments.en: Now do you have any advice that you can give our listeners about describing your last job?
segments.zh: 现在你有什么建议可以给我们的听众描述你的上一份工作吗？

segments.en: Why did you leave your previous employer?
segments.zh: 你为什么离开你以前的雇主？

segments.en: Well I do have a little bit of basic job advice.
segments.zh: 好吧，我确实有一些基本的工作建议。

segments.en: I would say don't complain about your last employer.
segments.zh: 我会说，不要抱怨你上一份工作的雇主。

segments.en: Don't say my boss was mean, my co-workers were lazy, my company was terrible because usually as a person doing an interview, that makes you think that this person, if they work for you, will complain about you.
segments.zh: 不要说我的老板很刻薄、我的同事很懒、我的公司很糟糕，因为作为面试官，这通常会让你觉得，这个人如果为你工作，也会抱怨你。

segments.en: And so I think it's important like what Rebecca does in this dialogue to keep it positive.
segments.zh: 所以我认为重要的是，就像丽贝卡在这次对话中所做的那样，要保持积极性。

segments.en: Every negative situation can become a positive experience.
segments.zh: 每一个消极的情况都可以成为一种积极的体验。

segments.en: So the job was tough but it was a good challenge, right?
segments.zh: 所以这份工作很艰难，但这是一个很好的挑战，对吧？

segments.en: Or but she learned how to do many new things.
segments.zh: 或者她学会了如何做许多新的事情。

segments.en: I think this is important for anybody in any language but in English especially to use some of these phrases and to say, you know, I really like a challenge or I didn't feel this was challenging enough, things like this.
segments.zh: 我认为这对任何语言的任何人都很重要，尤其是在英语中，特别是使用其中一些短语，并说，你知道，我真的很喜欢挑战，或者我觉得这不够具有挑战性，诸如此类。

segments.en: As opposed to, my old boss is so mean, he made me work on the weekends, that company is so terrible.
segments.zh: 相反，我的老老板是如此卑鄙，他让我在周末工作，那家公司太糟糕了。

segments.en: I mean that kind of stuff no one wants to hear.
segments.zh: 我的意思是没有人想听的那种东西。

segments.en: Yeah exactly and I think it's not really useful because even if the company is the competitor, so you don't really get any extra points for giving them like the dirty secrets of what was going on in the company.
segments.zh: 是的，而且我觉得这没什么用，因为即使那家公司是竞争对手，你把这些内幕、公司里发生的见不得人的事说出来，也得不到任何加分。

segments.en: Maybe saying, oh my co-workers, they were just so mean to me and stuff like this.
segments.zh: 也许会说，哦，我的同事，他们对我太刻薄了之类的。

segments.en: Yeah, no, it makes you seem like a complainer and no one wants to hire a complainer.
segments.zh: 是的，不，这会让你看起来像个爱抱怨的人，而没人想雇一个爱抱怨的人。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: Alright so this is an interesting topic we would like to hear from you.
segments.zh: 好吧，这是一个有趣的话题，我们想听听您的意见。

segments.en: So come to EnglishPod.com and tell us why did you leave your previous employer?
segments.zh: 所以来englishpod.com 告诉我们你为什么离开你以前的雇主？

segments.en: Or just let us know about some of your interview experiences or some of your interview questions.
segments.zh: 或者只是让我们知道您的一些面试经历或您的一些面试问题。

segments.en: We're happy to help you out.
segments.zh: 我们很乐意为您提供帮助。

segments.en: We'll hope to see you at the website.
segments.zh: 我们希望在网站上见到您。

segments.en: Alright we'll see you there.
segments.zh: 好的，我们会在那里见到你。

segments.en: Bye.
segments.zh: 再见。
